title: Bajaj Finance Shares Tumble 5.8% as RBI Draft Targets NBFC Revolving Credit Products
excerpt: A draft RBI proposal to curb revolving-credit products offered by non-bank lenders triggered the sharpest single-day fall in Bajaj Finance shares this year.
body:
• Bajaj Finance shares fell 5.8% on Friday after a draft RBI proposal raised concerns over restrictions on revolving-credit products offered by NBFCs.
  • The Reserve Bank of India is considering limits on certain revolving-credit instruments that have driven rapid growth at several non-bank lenders.
  • The decline made Bajaj Finance the biggest loser among non-bank lenders, dragging the broader financial sector lower.
  • The move follows a series of RBI actions to tighten oversight of the fast-growing NBFC sector.

Bajaj Finance shares tumbled 5.8% on Friday, leading losses among India's non-bank financial companies after a draft Reserve Bank of India proposal raised concerns over potential restrictions on revolving-credit products offered by the sector, Reuters reported.

What the RBI Proposal Covers

The central bank's draft guidelines target certain revolving-credit instruments that have become a significant growth driver for NBFCs like Bajaj Finance. While the full details of the proposal are still being finalised, the market interpreted the move as a signal that the RBI intends to rein in aggressive lending practices in the consumer credit space.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=sBMpC4qJdiE

Bajaj Finance's stock dropped from its previous close of Rs 1,149.90 to Rs 1,082, its steepest single-day decline this year. The parent company Bajaj Finserv also fell 3.7% in sympathy.

Pattern of Regulatory Tightening

The draft comes against a backdrop of sustained regulatory tightening in India's NBFC sector. In November 2023, the RBI barred Bajaj Finance from issuing loans under its eCOM and Insta EMI Card digital lending products for failing to disclose key information to borrowers. That action was eventually resolved after the company came into compliance.

More recently, the RBI has increased risk weights on certain unsecured loan categories, raised concerns about overleveraged borrowers and flagged rapid growth in consumer credit as a potential systemic risk. The central bank has also pushed NBFCs toward tighter asset-liability management and more conservative provisioning.

"This week was a mixed bag for markets. RBI's decision to keep rates unchanged was in line with expectations, while crash in crude oil prices earlier in the week on Mideast peace prospects helped sentiments."

— Sunny Agrawal, Head of Fundamental Equity Research, SBICAPS Securities

Market Impact and Broader Context

The sell-off in Bajaj Finance weighed on the broader market on a day when Indian benchmarks were already under pressure. The Nifty 50 fell 0.27% to 24,570.65 while the BSE Sensex dropped 0.58% to 78,499.17, trimming weekly gains.

Twelve of the 16 major sectors logged losses on Friday. Investors also stayed cautious ahead of US monthly jobs data, which could shape expectations for future Federal Reserve rate moves — a factor that influences foreign fund flows into Indian equities.

Foreign investors have bought a net $1.3 billion of Indian shares so far in August, following $2.1 billion in July, according to National Securities Depository data. The RBI's regulatory posture on NBFCs will be closely watched by overseas investors who have significant exposure to India's financial services sector.
nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to Indian financial stocks should monitor the RBI's evolving stance on NBFC lending practices, which could reshape the sector's growth trajectory.
